svg.text: THE CORE — SearchIndex, the one object that owns state
docLengths: Map<String, Integer> — for tf normalisation
smallest posting list first; OR ⇒ addAll
ReadWriteLock, not synchronized: search is 1000× more frequent
than indexing, so readers must not block each other ✓
it OWNS state but DELEGATES every policy — tokenizing,
scoring and side-effects all leave through a seam ✓
fuzzyExpand scans EVERY term in the index — O(V · |t|²). Needs an n-gram index.
THE rule: the SAME tokenizer must run on indexing AND on the query,
or a stemmed index will never match an unstemmed query.
it WRAPS a Tokenizer ⇒ this is
suffix-chopping, not a real Porter stemmer
lock ⇒ one slow listener stalls indexing
THE MODEL — value objects, all immutable
fields are separable ⇒ SearchField filtering is possible
operator: AND | OR · field: TITLE | CONTENT | TAGS | ALL
filters: Map · fuzzy: boolean · offset, limit
6 optional knobs ⇒ Builder beats a 6-arg constructor
no POSITIONS ⇒ phrase queries ("design patterns") impossible
avgDocLength is exactly what BM25's b term needs

g.text: FOUR PATTERNS, FOUR DIFFERENT AXES OF CHANGE
Strategy (ranking) — relevance model changes often, index does not.
Strategy/Decorator (tokenizer) — analysis chain is per-language.
Observer (index events) — cache, analytics and replication all
want the same signal, and none of them belong in SearchIndex.
Builder (SearchQuery) — six optional knobs, no telescoping ctor.
Name the axis of change, then the pattern. Not the other way round.
Template Method is claimed for the tokenizer, but the sketch actually
composes (StemmingTokenizer wraps a delegate) — say Decorator instead.

svg.text: ① SearchIndex + its two maps → ② Tokenizer seam (same on write AND read) → ③ RankingStrategy → ④ IndexObserver → ⑤ Document / SearchQuery+Builder / SearchResult / PostingList

DESIGN SPEC — no Java under problems/searchengine. Compiled cousin: simplesearch.
Read it as "what I would build", not "what already runs".
